topics.label: CIA Triad
topics.desc: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability — the core objectives against which every security control and tradeoff is measured.

topics.label: Threat Modeling
topics.desc: Systematic identification of assets, threats, and attack vectors (e.g. STRIDE) to prioritize defenses before code is written.

topics.label: Attack Surface
topics.desc: The sum of entry points an adversary can exploit; minimizing it reduces exposure and the cost of defending a system.

topics.label: Defense in Depth
topics.desc: Layering independent controls so that breach of one barrier does not compromise the whole system.

topics.label: Least Privilege
topics.desc: Granting each principal only the minimal rights needed, limiting blast radius when an account or component is compromised.

topics.label: Risk Management
topics.desc: Quantifying likelihood and impact of threats to decide what to mitigate, accept, transfer, or avoid within budget.

topics.label: Zero Trust
topics.desc: Architecture that trusts no implicit network position, verifying every request's identity, device, and context continuously.

topics.label: Symmetric Encryption
topics.desc: Shared-key ciphers like AES that encrypt bulk data efficiently; security hinges on secure key distribution and mode of operation.

topics.label: Public-Key Cryptography
topics.desc: Key-pair schemes (RSA, ECC) enabling encryption and signatures without shared secrets, underpinning TLS and PKI.

topics.label: Cryptographic Hashing
topics.desc: One-way collision-resistant functions (SHA-2/3) giving fixed-size digests for integrity, fingerprints, and commitments.

topics.label: Digital Signatures
topics.desc: Asymmetric authentication providing integrity and non-repudiation by signing a hash with a private key.

topics.label: Key Exchange
topics.desc: Protocols like Diffie-Hellman that derive shared secrets over insecure channels, enabling forward secrecy in TLS.

topics.label: PKI & Certificates
topics.desc: Hierarchies of certificate authorities binding public keys to identities, the trust backbone for TLS and code signing.

topics.label: Password Hashing
topics.desc: Slow salted KDFs (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2) that resist offline brute-force attacks on stored credentials.

topics.label: Crypto Pitfalls
topics.desc: Common failures — ECB mode, nonce reuse, rolling your own crypto, weak RNGs — that silently break otherwise sound primitives.

topics.label: OWASP Top 10
topics.desc: The industry-standard list of the most critical web application risks, a baseline checklist for appsec triage and training.

topics.label: Injection Attacks
topics.desc: Untrusted input interpreted as code (SQLi, command, LDAP), letting attackers alter queries; prevented by parameterization.

topics.label: Cross-Site Scripting
topics.desc: Injecting attacker script into pages (stored, reflected, DOM) to hijack sessions; mitigated by output encoding and CSP.

topics.label: CSRF
topics.desc: Forging authenticated cross-origin requests using ambient credentials; defended with anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.

topics.label: SSRF
topics.desc: Tricking a server into making attacker-controlled requests, reaching internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

topics.label: Insecure Deserialization
topics.desc: Untrusted serialized data triggering object instantiation that leads to remote code execution or logic abuse.

topics.label: Broken Access Control
topics.desc: Missing authorization checks (IDOR, path traversal) letting users reach data or actions outside their permissions.

topics.label: Authentication
topics.desc: Verifying a principal's claimed identity via factors like passwords, keys, or biometrics before granting access.

topics.label: Authorization
topics.desc: Deciding what an authenticated principal may do, enforced through models like RBAC, ABAC, or policy engines.

topics.label: Multi-Factor Auth
topics.desc: Combining factors from distinct categories (know/have/are) so a single stolen credential cannot grant access.

topics.label: OAuth 2.0 & OIDC
topics.desc: Delegated authorization and federated identity standards underpinning third-party login and API access tokens.

topics.label: Session Management
topics.desc: Issuing, storing, and invalidating session tokens or JWTs securely to bind requests to an authenticated user.

topics.label: RBAC & ABAC
topics.desc: Role- and attribute-based access models that scale permission management across large user and resource sets.

topics.label: Federation & SSO
topics.desc: Single sign-on via SAML or OIDC so one identity provider authenticates users across many relying applications.

topics.label: Firewalls
topics.desc: Packet- and application-layer filters enforcing allow/deny policy at network boundaries and between segments.

topics.label: TLS
topics.desc: The protocol securing data in transit with authenticated encryption and forward secrecy, foundation of HTTPS.

topics.label: Network Segmentation
topics.desc: Partitioning networks into zones to contain lateral movement and enforce least-privilege traffic flows.

topics.label: IDS / IPS
topics.desc: Systems that detect or block malicious traffic using signatures and anomaly analysis at network choke points.

topics.label: DDoS Defense
topics.desc: Absorbing or filtering volumetric and application-layer floods via rate limiting, scrubbing, and anycast capacity.

topics.label: VPN & Tunneling
topics.desc: Encrypted tunnels (IPsec, WireGuard) extending trusted networks over untrusted links for remote and site-to-site access.

topics.label: Cloud Network Security
topics.desc: Securing VPCs, security groups, and service meshes where the perimeter is software-defined and identity-driven.

topics.label: Secure SDLC
topics.desc: Embedding security activities — threat modeling, review, testing — across every phase of the development lifecycle.

topics.label: Input Validation
topics.desc: Rejecting or constraining untrusted input against strict allowlists, the first defense against injection and abuse.

topics.label: Secrets Management
topics.desc: Storing and rotating credentials in vaults rather than code, preventing leaked keys from compromising systems.

topics.label: Dependency Security
topics.desc: Scanning and pinning third-party packages to catch known vulnerabilities and supply-chain tampering in the build.

topics.label: SAST & DAST
topics.desc: Static and dynamic analysis tooling that surfaces code-level and running-app vulnerabilities in CI pipelines.

topics.label: Secure Defaults
topics.desc: Shipping configurations that are safe out of the box, so security does not depend on every operator opting in.

topics.label: Software Supply Chain
topics.desc: Securing the build and distribution path — provenance, SBOMs, signed artifacts — against compromise like SolarWinds.

topics.label: SIEM & Log Analysis
topics.desc: Centralizing and correlating event logs to detect attacks and support investigation across the estate.

topics.label: Incident Response
topics.desc: The structured process — detect, contain, eradicate, recover — for handling breaches and minimizing damage.

topics.label: Vulnerability Management
topics.desc: Continuous discovery, prioritization (CVSS), and remediation of weaknesses across assets before they are exploited.

topics.label: Penetration Testing
topics.desc: Authorized adversarial simulation to find exploitable flaws that automated scanners and reviews miss.

topics.label: Threat Intelligence
topics.desc: Collecting and applying knowledge of adversaries' TTPs and IOCs to anticipate and detect targeted attacks.

topics.label: Security Monitoring
topics.desc: Continuous detection via alerts, EDR, and dashboards to surface malicious activity early in the kill chain.

topics.label: Digital Forensics
topics.desc: Preserving and analyzing evidence after an incident to reconstruct attacker actions and support legal action.

topics.label: Encryption at Rest
topics.desc: Protecting stored data with disk, database, or field-level encryption so theft of media does not expose contents.

topics.label: Data Classification
topics.desc: Labeling data by sensitivity to drive proportionate controls for handling, retention, and access.

topics.label: Privacy Regulations
topics.desc: Legal regimes like GDPR and CCPA mandating consent, data-subject rights, and breach disclosure for personal data.

topics.label: Masking & Tokenization
topics.desc: Replacing sensitive fields with non-sensitive surrogates so analytics and lower environments avoid exposing real data.

topics.label: Data Loss Prevention
topics.desc: Policies and tooling that detect and block exfiltration of sensitive data across endpoints, network, and storage.

topics.label: Anonymization
topics.desc: Removing or perturbing identifiers (k-anonymity, differential privacy) to enable data use without re-identification.

topics.label: Key Management
topics.desc: Lifecycle of cryptographic keys — generation, rotation, storage in HSMs/KMS — on which all encryption ultimately depends.
